points.reason: The reg_file storage in this generate branch is forwarded to operand-read processes and can therefore be observed through the operand outputs, while this block only forces register zero to a constant and has no independent attacker-controlled overwrite.
This process stores reg_file values that are later returned by the operand-read processes, and rd_i or reset can overwrite those stored values.
The FPGA register-file process writes rd_i into reg_file and directly reads selected reg_file values into rs1_o and rs2_o.
rf_we gates writes and opa_addr selects the register written or read, so the control logic can redirect or suppress modification of the stored contents.
The process exposes reg_file through rs1_o and rs2_o, while rf_rs1 and rf_rs2 select which stored values are released and can therefore steer the returned operands.
rs3_addr selects the reg_file entry returned through rs3_o, allowing the released register value to be redirected.
The process reads a selected reg_file entry into rs3_o, and the selection control can change which register content is returned.
opa_addr selects the register index for the write and first-operand read, and the control fields choose which address source is used.
The rf_rd field is compared with each generated register index, so changing it redirects the write destination.
opa_addr is used as an index for both the FPGA write and the first-operand read, so it can select an unintended register.
The rf_rs1 field selects the reg_file element returned on rs1_o, allowing the first operand address to produce an unintended value.
